findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization path renders a hardcoded empty table
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` organization feature is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` with completely hardcoded empty data instead of the actual `result.data`/`result.meta` from the query. The flagged branch also ignores `loading` (no placeholder while loading), errors, `title`, and the `getCustomFieldRenderer`/`fieldHeaderMap` wiring that the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` path uses. The moment anyone enables this flag for an organization, every table-type dashboard widget will render an empty table with zero columns and no loading state, silently hiding all data. Either wire the real `tableResults` data through or don't merge the flag check until the visualization actually consumes query results.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present
findings.body: The new `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES = ['is_segment', 'project_id', 'received']` list is applied inside the memo like this: `if (!searchQuery.trim()) { return sorted; }` followed by `sorted.filter(attribute => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name) && ...)`. Because the early return happens for the empty-search case, the hidden attributes are only excluded while the user is actively typing a search query. In the default attribute view (no search entered), `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still rendered, which defeats the purpose of the hidden list. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` predicate should be applied to `sorted` regardless of whether a search query is present.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results positionally, which is not order-safe
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, and then builds events via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id and does not guarantee that `.values()` comes back in the same order as the requested `node_ids` (and missing keys may be omitted or set to `None`, shifting subsequent pairs). As a result, the `id` recorded on each `ErrorEvent` can be paired with a different event's data. Today the downstream log generation only reads `title`/`message`/`timestamp` (which come from the same data object), so the user-facing impact is currently limited to the latent `id` field being wrong, but the pairing should be done by iterating the node ids and looking up `events[node_id]` instead of relying on positional zip.
